title: Self-Debiasing Large Language Models: Zero-Shot Recognition and Reduction of Stereotypes
measurement_description: The paper measured 'bias scores' for 'stereotyping' in Large Language Models within religious contexts, specifically evaluating the frequency with which the LLM's answers aligned with attested stereotypes. It identified invalid assumptions related to religious groups in question-answering tasks.
findings: For the 'Religion' social group, the baseline bias score for GPT-3.5 Turbo was 0.063 (95% CI: 0.032, 0.094). While both self-debiasing techniques (explanation and reprompting) reduced the raw bias scores to 0.050 (95% CI: 0.025, 0.075) and 0.029 (95% CI: 0.000, 0.056) respectively, these reductions were not statistically significant, as their 95% confidence intervals overlapped with the baseline. This contrasts with most other social groups where significant bias reductions were observed.
